items.front: GDP vs GNP — the one-line difference?
items.back: GDP = output within borders (residents + foreigners). GNP = output by residents anywhere = GDP + NFIA.
items.examPoint: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: What exactly is 'National Income'?
items.back: NNP at Factor Cost = NNP(MP) − Indirect Taxes + Subsidies — income accruing to factors of production.
items.examPoint: NI = NNP at Factor Cost; Personal & Disposable Income
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: The two 'knobs' converting GDP to National Income?
items.back: Add NFIA (domestic→national); subtract Depreciation (gross→net); then MP→FC (−IT +subsidies).
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: Market Price → Factor Cost conversion?
items.back: Factor Cost = Market Price − Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.
items.examPoint: Market price vs Factor cost (indirect taxes − subsidies)
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: GDP deflator formula and what it measures?
items.back: (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100 — broadest price index, covers all goods/services in GDP (unlike CPI/WPI).
items.examPoint: Nominal vs Real GDP & GDP deflator
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: The three methods of estimating national income?
items.back: Product/value-added (output−intermediate); Income (wages+rent+interest+profit+mixed); Expenditure (C+I+G+(X−M)).
items.examPoint: GVA & three methods of national income estimation
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: Which incomes are EXCLUDED in the income method?
items.back: Transfer payments (pensions, scholarships) — no corresponding production.
items.examPoint: Income Method (factor incomes; transfer payments excluded)
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: GVA-to-GDP relationship?
items.back: GDP(market price) = GVA(basic prices) + Product Taxes − Product Subsidies; GVA headlined since 2015.
items.examPoint: GVA — concept & GVA-to-GDP relation (headline metric since 2015)
items.source: MoSPI National Accounts

items.front: Current base year and the upcoming new series?
items.back: 2022-23 (new series released 27 Feb 2026, replacing 2011-12); guided by ACNAS (Goldar), NSO-MoSPI; uses GST/MCA-21/PLFS.
items.examPoint: Base year — 2022-23 new series (released Feb 2026, replaced 2011-12; ACNAS, NSO-MoSPI)
items.source: MoSPI / PIB

items.front: Who made the earliest vs first scientific estimate of India's national income?
items.back: Earliest — Dadabhai Naoroji (1867-68); first scientific — V.K.R.V. Rao (1931).
items.examPoint: History & agencies — Dadabhai Naoroji, V.K.R.V. Rao, CSO/NSO, NSC; estimation difficulties
items.source: Standard Indian Economy ref

items.front: Disposable Income formula?
items.back: DI = Personal Income − direct/personal taxes (what households can spend or save).
items.examPoint: NI = NNP at Factor Cost; Personal & Disposable Income
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: If NFIA is negative, how do GNP and GDP compare (India's usual case)?
items.back: GNP < GDP — outflows to foreign investors exceed residents' earnings abroad.
items.source: APPSC GK — National Income

items.front: Is national income a stock or a flow?
items.back: A flow — measured over a period (a year). Capital and wealth are stocks (measured at a point of time).

items.front: What makes a good final rather than intermediate?
items.back: Its use: bought for consumption or investment = final; bought for resale or further processing = intermediate. The same good can be either.

items.front: Who is a normal resident in national accounting?
items.back: A person or institution whose centre of economic interest lies in the country (usually living there a year or more).

items.front: Value of output in national accounting?
items.back: Value of output = sales + change in stock (inventories).

items.front: Formula for the GDP growth rate?
items.back: (GDP this year − GDP last year) ÷ GDP last year × 100; use real GDP for economic growth.

items.front: Formula for per capita income?
items.back: Per capita income = National income ÷ Population — a rough gauge of average living standards.
